content: Omeprazole is a medication prescribed to treat various conditions related to excessive stomach acid production. It is used alone or in combination with other medications to manage stomach or small intestine ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and erosive esophagitis. GERD is a condition where stomach acid flows backward into the esophagus, causing heartburn and potential damage to the esophageal lining. Erosive esophagitis involves inflammation and erosion of the esophageal lining. Omeprazole is also used to treat conditions where the stomach produces too much acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Additionally, it is prescribed with other medications to eradicate Helicobacter pylori (a bacteria that causes ulcers) and prevent the recurrence of ulcers in patients with a history of small intestine ulcers. Omeprazole is available in various forms, including delayed-release capsules, nonprescription delayed-release tablets, powder for suspension, and regular capsules. The powder and regular capsules contain sodium bicarbonate, which reduces stomach acid and enhances the rapid action of omeprazole. Delayed-release capsules are typically taken once daily before a meal, but they may be taken twice daily when used to eliminate H. pylori or up to three times daily for conditions involving excessive stomach acid production. The capsules are usually taken in the morning on an empty stomach, one hour before a meal. The powder is also taken once daily on an empty stomach, either in the morning or at bedtime. Nonprescription delayed-release tablets are taken once daily in the morning before eating, for a 14-day course, which can be repeated every four months if necessary. To ensure proper use, follow the instructions on your prescription or package label carefully. Take omeprazole exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless advised by your doctor. Swallow regular capsules with water, avoiding other liquids. Swallow delayed-release capsules, regular capsules, and nonprescription tablets whole; do not split, chew, or crush them. Do not mix nonprescription tablets with food or open regular capsules to mix their contents with food. If you have difficulty swallowing delayed-release capsules, you may mix the contents with one tablespoon of cool applesauce and swallow the mixture immediately with a glass of cool water. Do not chew or crush the pellets, and do not store the mixture for future use. If you are using the powder form, mix it with 1-2 tablespoons of water in a small cup, stir well, and drink immediately. Refill the cup with water and drink again to ensure all medication is consumed. Do not mix the powder with other liquids or food. Ensure you are taking the correct strength and number of capsules or powder packets as prescribed. For example, if prescribed one 40 mg capsule or packet, do not substitute it with two 20 mg capsules or packets. Consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions about your dosage. Nonprescription omeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn symptoms, as it may take 1-4 days to achieve its full effect. Contact your doctor if your symptoms worsen, do not improve after 14 days, or return sooner than four months after completing treatment. Do not use nonprescription omeprazole for more than 14 days or more frequently than once every four months without consulting your doctor. Your doctor may prescribe omeprazole for 10-14 days to eliminate H. pylori or for 4-8 weeks or longer to treat other conditions. Continue taking omeprazole even if you feel well, and do not stop taking prescription omeprazole without consulting your doctor. Before taking omeprazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to omeprazole, esomeprazole, lansoprazole, pantoprazole, rabeprazole, or any other medications or ingredients in the type of omeprazole you will be taking. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Mention specific medications such as ampicillin, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), atazanavir, cyclosporine, diazepam, digoxin, disulfiram, ketoconazole, medications for anxiety or seizures, phenytoin, sedatives, sleeping pills, tacrolimus, tranquilizers, and iron-containing vitamins or supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. If you are taking regular capsules or powder, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had low calcium or potassium levels in your blood or excessive vomiting. Your doctor may advise against taking omeprazole capsules or powder. If you plan to take nonprescription omeprazole, inform your doctor if your heartburn has lasted three months or longer or if you have experienced symptoms such as lightheadedness, sweating, dizziness, chest or shoulder pain, shortness of breath, pain spreading to your arms, neck, or shoulders, unexplained weight loss, nausea, vomiting (especially vomiting blood), stomach pain, difficulty swallowing, or black or bloody stools. These symptoms may indicate a more serious condition that cannot be treated with nonprescription medication. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking omeprazole, contact your doctor. For patients taking regular capsules or powder, your doctor may recommend limiting the intake of milk and other calcium-rich foods and drinks during treatment. Follow these instructions carefully. If you are taking other forms of omeprazole, continue your normal diet unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Omeprazole may cause side effects. Mild side effects include stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation, dizziness, cough, and back pain. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects include rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, difficulty breathing or swallowing, hoarseness, seizures, muscle spasms or cramps, and burning or tingling sensations in the lips, tongue, hands, or feet. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while taking this medication. Store omeprazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from light, heat, and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include confusion, drowsiness, blurred vision, rapid or pounding heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, sweating, flushing, headache, and dry mouth. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you are taking prescription omeprazole, consult your pharmacist with any questions about refilling your prescription.
